environment.description: Same application deployed on RHEL 9 with a custom SELinux type enforcement module (converter_app_t). The policy module was generated via audit2allow from a training run and then manually tightened. The process runs in confined domain converter_app_t with type transitions. File context rules: /tmp/convert_* files receive type converter_tmp_t. The policy allows converter_app_t to create/read/write/unlink files of type converter_tmp_t ONLY. Other processes (including those in unconfined_t, user_t, or container_t domains) have NO read/write access to converter_tmp_t labeled files. Additionally, converter_app_t is denied mknod, symlink creation in /tmp, and cannot transition file labels. The /tmp directory itself has tmp_t context and the process cannot write to tmp_t directly - only through the automatic type_transition rule that assigns converter_tmp_t to new files. Inter-process communication via /tmp is blocked because no other domain has allow rules for converter_tmp_t.

allow_rules: allow converter_app_t converter_tmp_t:file { create read write unlink getattr open };
allow converter_app_t tmp_t:dir { add_name remove_name write search };
config.deny_other_domains: No other domain has allow rules for converter_tmp_t objects
config.additional_restrictions: neverallow converter_app_t tmp_t:file { write create }; neverallow converter_app_t self:capability { mknod }; neverallow unconfined_t converter_tmp_t:file { read write };
config.file_permissions_note: DAC permissions 0666 are set but MAC policy takes precedence
